title: How the Eukaryotyping distance ensemble works
text: Let \(\mathbf{v}_{ij}\) allele values (set, actual observed alleles, multiplicities) carried isolate \(\) locus \(j\), let \(p_{ja}\) empirical frequency allele \(\) . Hypothesis 0 — unrelated: isolates draw alleles independently locus allele frequencies: \[ \ell_0 = \sum_{\\mathbf{v}_{ij}} \log p_{ja} +           \sum_{\\mathbf{v}_{kj}} \log p_{ja} \] Hypothesis 1 — share one allele: pair shares exactly one allele; shared allele likely one. every pair positions \((u, v)\) \(v_{iju} = v_{kjv}\), compute: \[ \ell_{1,uv} = \ell_0 - \log p_{j,v_{iju}} \] take \(\ell_1 = \max_{uv} \ell_{1,uv}\). shared allele exists, \(\ell_1 = \log(\epsilon \cdot \min(p_{\text{obs}}))\), \(\epsilon\) estimated allele-capture failure rate (default 0.3072, estimated Joel Barratt May 2019) \(\min(p_{\text{obs}})\) smallest frequency among alleles carried pair. Hypothesis 2 — share alleles: isolates share pair alleles (multiset equality). every pair 2-subsets \((\mathbf{}, \mathbf{b})\) \(\mathbf{v}_{ij}\) \(\mathbf{v}_{kj}\) equal multisets: \[ \ell_{2,\mathbf{}\mathbf{b}} =   \sum_{\\mathbf{v}_{ij} \setminus \mathbf{}} \log p_{ja} +   \sum_{\\mathbf{v}_{kj}} \log p_{ja} \] equivalent \(\ell_0\) log-frequencies removed pair elements subtracted (original R code uses match() locate first-position index pair value, removes indices via negative indexing). Let \[ n_{\text{shared}} = \max_{\mathbf{},\mathbf{b}}   \bigl|\operatorname{intersect}(\mathbf{}, \mathbf{b})\bigr| \] maximum distinct-allele overlap 2-subset combinations. multiset equality found, \(\ell_2 = \max \ell_{2,\mathbf{}\mathbf{b}}\). Otherwise: \[ \ell_2 = \log\bigl[(\epsilon \cdot \min(p_{\text{obs}}))^{2 - n_{\text{shared}}}\bigr] \] ploidy 1 loci, either allele vector length 1, package sets \(\ell_2 = \ell_1\) (package-level decision — original script crashes cases).

title: How the Eukaryotyping distance ensemble works
text: per-locus log-likelihoods summed across loci: \[ s_0 = \sum_{j} \ell_0^{(j)}, \quad s_1 = \sum_{j} \ell_1^{(j)}, \quad s_2 = \sum_{j} \ell_2^{(j)} \] normalised posterior three hypotheses: \[ \Pr(h \mid \text{data}) = \frac{e^{s_h}}{e^{s_0} + e^{s_1} + e^{s_2}}, \quad h \\{0, 1, 2\} \] distance posterior expected number shared-allele hypotheses: \[ D_{ik}^{(B)} = 0 \cdot \Pr(0) + 1 \cdot \Pr(1) + 2 \cdot \Pr(2) \[0, 2] \] Values near 0 indicate pair appears unrelated; values near 2 suggest complete allelic sharing. Self-pair diagonals range approximately \(1.46\)–\(2.0\) (homozygous diploid common alleles scores near 2; singleton diploid rare allele scores lower).

title: How the Eukaryotyping distance ensemble works
text: Reproduces published run.r workflow verbatim: Reverse Bayesian direction: \(D_B' = 2 - D_B\) matrices divergence-oriented (larger = dissimilar). Min-max normalise matrix entries (diagonal, upper lower triangles together) \([0, 1]\). Let \(H\) normalised heuristic \(B\) reversed- normalised Bayesian matrix. Sort \(B\)’s values map onto rank-order \(H\): \[ D_{ik}^{(E)} = B_{(\text{rank}(H_{ik}))} \] ties \(H\) broken randomly (ties.method = "random"), making output non-deterministic unless seed provided. Take elementwise mean distribution-mapped matrix \(H\), rescale global maximum. ties heuristic ranking resolved random, two calls data can produce different matrices. output matrix can also asymmetric (random tie-breaking full-matrix (non-triangular) sorting guarantee symmetry).

title: How the Eukaryotyping distance ensemble works
text: package-specific variant avoids random tie-breaking preserves symmetry: Reverse Bayesian direction: \(D_B' = 2 - D_B\), matrices divergence-oriented. \(n \times n\) distance matrix \(D\), let \(U\) set \(\binom{n}{2}\) strictly upper-triangular entries. Assign fractional ranks: \[ r(D)_{ik} = \frac{\text{rank } D_{ik} \text{ among } U}                  {\binom{n}{2} + 1} \] ties resolved ties.method = "average". diagonal set NA. ensemble entry : \[ D_{ik}^{(E)} = \frac{r(D_H)_{ik} + r(D_B')_{ik}}{2} \]

what: What is MLST and why distance matrices?
title: Introduction to fasteukaryotyping
text: Multilocus Sequence Typing (MLST) characterises microbial isolates alleles present set housekeeping loci. Given collection samples (isolates), potentially multiple alleles per locus (due heterozygosity, mixed infections, polyploidy), central question : genetically similar two samples? fasteukaryotyping implements three-method ensemble described Barratt et al. (2019) (doi:10.1017/S0031182019000581) computing pairwise genetic distances MLST haplotype data sheets (HDS).
code: library(fasteukaryotyping)

title: Introduction to fasteukaryotyping
text: Barratt’s unsupervised heuristic mixture-model distance computes, locus, delta value depends number shared alleles, allele-set sizes, per-locus entropy term \(H_{\nu}\), frequency-informed penalty \(P\). per-locus deltas summed across loci produce pairwise distance. Missing loci imputed two-pass mean procedure matches original Barratt script.
code: set.seed(42) n <- 10 geno <- list(   matrix(sample(c(1L, 2L, 3L, NA), n * 2, replace = TRUE), nrow = n, ncol = 2),   matrix(sample(c(1L, 2L, NA), n * 2, replace = TRUE), nrow = n, ncol = 2) ) d_h <- euk_heuristic_distance(geno, ploidy = c(2L, 2L)) dim(d_h) ## [1] 10 10

title: Introduction to fasteukaryotyping
text: Plucinski’s naive Bayes genetic distance evaluates, pair locus, three log-likelihoods: ll0: samples unrelated – every allele drawn independently locus allele frequencies. ll1: samples share exactly one allele – shared allele likely one; remaining alleles drawn independently. ll2 (diploid loci ): samples share alleles – evaluated 2-subsets; missing allele draws get probability \(\epsilon \cdot \min(p_1, p_2)\). per-locus values summed, normalised posterior three hypotheses, distance posterior expectation \([0, 2]\).
code: d_b <- euk_bayesian_distance(geno, ploidy = c(2L, 2L)) dim(d_b) ## [1] 10 10

title: Introduction to fasteukaryotyping
text: ensemble converts matrix fractional ranks unordered pairs takes mean two ranks. copula-style average invariant monotone transformations either distance, producing consensus value \([0, 1]\).
code: d_e <- euk_ensemble_distance(geno, ploidy = c(2L, 2L)) dim(d_e) ## [1] 10 10

title: Introduction to fasteukaryotyping
text: core input geno list \(L\) integer matrices (one per locus), \(n\) rows (samples) maxMOI columns. Missing alleles coded NA (0). ploidy vector specifies whether locus haploid (1) diploid (2).
